Detailed method

These are sourdough baguettes, not the yeasted sticks. Currently 500 g flour, 68% hydration, 20% starter, 2% salt, and 0% yeast. That is 340 g water, 100 g starter, 10 g salt, and 0 g yeast, 950 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 70.9% effective hydration. Currently 4 sticks of 237.5 g. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Starter Use 100 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total. The yeast amount is 0 g.
  2. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 340 g water, the 100 g starter, 0 g instant yeast, and 10 g salt until no dry flour remains. At 68% the dough is soft. Fold it instead of kneading hard. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  3. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for about 3 to 4 hours. Give it three gentle folds in the first 90 minutes. It is ready when it has grown by about half and looks bubbly.
  4. Divide Divide the 950 g dough into 4 pieces of 237.5 g. Pre-shape each one into a loose log, cover, and rest 20 minutes.
  5. Shape Roll each log into a stick about 35 cm long. Set them seam-side down on a floured cloth, with a fold of cloth between them. The default 950 g uses a baking tray or baking stone about 40 cm long. If you change the amount, use a longer tray in proportion or bake in two batches.
  6. Proof Cover them for 40 to 60 minutes, until they look puffy. With 20% starter they need longer than yeasted sticks.
  7. Bake Heat the oven to 240°C (465°F). Score each stick on a diagonal three or four times. Bake 20 to 25 minutes with steam, until the crust is golden and the scores have opened. Cool on a rack.
